credentials.description: client_id of the environment (sandbox: developer account dashboard; production: Settings → API Keys, v4)

example_prompt: Release or cancel a deferred or scheduled Flutterwave payout, or move its scheduled date.

id.description: Path parameter. ID of the transfer

initiate.description: Used to initiate a deferred or scheduled transfer

close.description: Used to close a deferred or scheduled transfer.

disburse_option.description: To specify the date and time for disbursement, this is required when action is set to scheduled.

date_time.description: the scheduled date and time for when the transfer should be disbursed to the recipient's account. It should be in the 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' 24hr format.

id.description: The unique identifier for the transfer.

action.description: Specifies if the transfer is processed immediately or later.

status.description: The current status of the transfer. `NEW` indicates the transfer is being processed, while `CANCELLED` indicates the transfer has been cancelled.

disburse_option.description: To specify the date and time for disbursement, this is required when action is set to scheduled.

date_time.description: the scheduled date and time for when the transfer should be disbursed to the recipient's account. It should be in the 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' 24hr format.

updated_datetime.description: The date and time when the transfer was submitted for processing.

message.description: Present on 401/403/409 bodies; the 400 body has none.

type.description: Error category. Generic: REQUEST_NOT_VALID, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, RESOURCE_CONFLICT, UNPROCESSABLE, INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR; or a domain type (see code).

code.description: String. Generic 10400/10401/10403/10404/10409/10422/10500, or a domain code documented for this endpoint: 302400 INVALID_TRANSFER_STATUS (not in NEW status), 303400 TRANSFER_NOT_DEFERRED_SCHEDULED, 304400 TIME_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, 208400 INVALID_DISBURSE_ACTION.

gotchas: Auth: one token server for both environments — the docs' Multi-Environment Integrations example sends either environment's credentials to https://idp.flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token, and Authentication says "This process applies to both the sandbox and production environments. Make sure to use the correct credentials for each environment to obtain a valid token." "Each token is valid for **10 minutes**"; "We recommend refreshing the token at least one minute before it expires." Cache the token. Sandbox: "We archive your test data after 30 days."

Headers: X-Trace-Id is optional on this PUT (the headers guide lists it under 'Optional API Headers'; "It must be a string using only alphanumeric ASCII characters.", 12-255 characters). The API reference documents no X-Idempotency-Key for this endpoint.
Body (API reference): initiate: true releases a deferred or scheduled transfer, close: true cancels it, disburse_option reschedules it. Only works while the transfer is NEW and deferred or scheduled.

Open question: the guides describe a different body: Docs (General Transfer Flow): "setting `action` to `instant` to process the transfer or  set it to `close` to cancel it." The API reference schema has no action field; follow the reference and verify in sandbox.
The API reference lists 200/400/401/403 (no 409): wrong-state errors are the 30x400 codes above.

Errors: {"status":"failed","error":{"type","code","message","validation_errors"}}; error.code is a string and 400s carry validation_errors[{field_name,message}]. Besides the generic codes (10400 REQUEST_NOT_VALID, 10401, 10403 FORBIDDEN, 10404 RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND, 10409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT, 10422 UNPROCESSABLE, 10500) the error table documents these for this endpoint: 302400 INVALID_TRANSFER_STATUS (not in NEW status), 303400 TRANSFER_NOT_DEFERRED_SCHEDULED, 304400 TIME_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, 208400 INVALID_DISBURSE_ACTION. Branch on error.type / error.code, not on the HTTP status alone. Docs (Errors): "The current limit is 500 API requests per minute." A 429 can come back as a non-JSON page ("HTML error pages such as `Cloudflare 1015 responses`"): parse error bodies defensively and back off exponentially with jitter.
open_questions: Token URL: the PHP sample of Authentication uses https://keycloak.dev-flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token; its curl and JavaScript samples and the Multi-Environment example use https://idp.flutterwave.com/realms/flutterwave/protocol/openid-connect/token, which this spec follows.

spans: This can only be used to update instructions about a deferred payout.
